text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest open PR first. It catches routing errors before they hit users, saving time and trust. The trade-off is delayed feedback for the PR author, but catching issues early outweighs that cost.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow mode on open PRs risks slowing down reviews by adding noise to every PR, not just the newest—authors may ignore critical feedback if it’s buried in false positives. Instead, run PR-Agent in shadow mode on a random 10% of merged PRs weekly to catch systemic issues without disrupting workflows; if error rates spike, expand coverage. Settle it by measuring review time impact and false positive rate over two weeks.

name: Overhaul
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest *merged* PR first, not open—this catches routing errors in code that’s already proven stable, cutting false positives while still spotting systemic flaws. Skip the newest open PR entirely; merged PRs give real-world data without slowing down active reviews.

name: Sprocket
text: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest merged PR first. This catches routing errors in code that’s already proven stable, cutting false positives while still spotting systemic flaws. The trade-off is delayed detection—issues in open PRs won’t surface as quickly—but merged PRs give real-world data without slowing down active reviews.

name: Ratchet
text:
DECISION: Run PR-Agent in shadow mode on the newest merged PR first, then expand to weekly random 10% of merged PRs if results prove useful.

Result: A report showing routing errors caught and false positives reduced, owned by Overhaul.
